title: FedPurify: Knowledge-Preserving Backdoor Defense with Data-Free Purification in Federated Learning

problem.claim: Federated learning is vulnerable to backdoor attacks.

gap.claim: Existing defenses can sacrifice task-relevant knowledge and reduce clean-task accuracy by suppressing or discarding malicious updates.

contributions.claim: FedPurify performs post-training, data-free purification to remove malicious backdoors while preserving task-relevant knowledge.
FedPurify synthesizes diverse representative samples from a converged global model without using data and applies data-free trigger inversion to expose latent backdoor behaviors.
FedPurify uses contrastive feature alignment together with knowledge-preserving self-distillation to eliminate backdoor effects while retaining benign task performance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments verify effective backdoor removal with negligible impact on clean performance.
The authors report that FedPurify outperforms existing defense methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning faces vulnerability to backdoor attacks.
Existing robust-aggregation and detection-based defenses suppress or discard malicious updates, potentially reducing clean-task accuracy.
FedPurify performs post-training data-free purification intended to remove backdoors while preserving task-relevant knowledge.
The framework synthesizes samples from the converged global model, inverts triggers, and combines feature alignment with self-distillation.
The authors report effective backdoor removal, negligible clean-performance impact, and improvement over existing defenses.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, attack configurations, model architectures, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe computational costs or the conditions under which clean performance remains unaffected.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported experimental findings.
